markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) The diagnosis suggests weak aggregation of repeated recent interests. Training margins cannot establish whether those interests influence recommendations. (2) Broad relevance can conceal unsupported compatibility assumptions. Available titles/descriptions support limited evidence checks, with missing specifications requiring abstention. (3) The adapter exposes architecture-independent scoring hooks. Controlled history interventions can therefore remain comparable when the encoder changes.

**Related work.** (1) CETRec separates recency from relative order [1]. This motivates testing evidence removal separately from sequence rearrangement. (2) Sampling-reliability research distinguishes sampled ranking from full-catalog evaluation [2]. Pinned macro validation HR@10 must remain the selection criterion. (3) TREC’s relationship vocabulary separates compatibility from complementarity [3]. Diagnostic labels should preserve “unknown” rather than infer ownership or replacement needs.

### Directions and framework

| Direction | Existing signal | Proposed addition | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interest aggregation | Training margins | Matched history masking | Model dependence |
| Temporal reasoning | Sequence scores | Order-only perturbations | Positional sensitivity |
| Product usefulness | Text similarity | Evidence spans and abstention | Documented compatibility only |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Matched evidence masking** [1] | 5: + controlled combination; − familiar interventions | 8: + actionable diagnosis; − observational interests | 3: + existing hooks; − matching details |
| Recency-weighted history residual added to SASRec | 4: + targeted aggregation; − standard pooling | 7: + inexpensive ablation; − may amplify redundant interests | 4: + small module; − predictor changes |
| Text-supported compatibility audit [3] | 5: + explicit abstention; − established taxonomy | 6: + interpretable errors; − sparse specifications | 6: + simple rules possible; − annotation burden |

### Selected idea: matched evidence masking

At 0% progress, establish a trustworthy diagnostic before changing training. Using training histories only, identify repeated recent interest clusters through TF–IDF similarity of available titles/descriptions; treat clusters as proxies, not verified intentions. Compare masking cluster events against equal-size random event sets matched by position bins and training-item popularity. Separately test isolated-event masking and prefix shuffling that preserves the latest item.

```text
cache original recommendation scores
for each eligible history:
    identify repeated recent evidence and matched controls
    mask events in place, preserving position indices
    rescore through compatibility view
    record rank changes and top-10 overlap
aggregate paired differences within each category
```

Require position-preserving attention masks; zero padding alone may change encoder behavior. Report eligible counts, missing text, matched-control balance, and unavailable statistics explicitly. Use category-stratified user bootstrap intervals; repeated interventions remain grouped by user. These measurements establish model dependence, not user causality. Keep twenty-user full-catalog feedback exploratory and select subsequent model changes exclusively through pinned macro validation HR@10.

References: [1] [CETRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047); [2] [Sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086); [3] [TREC recommendations](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html).

idea.description: Implement matched evidence masking in the compatibility-preserving DiagnosisProbe to measure dependence on repeated recent interests versus isolated interactions.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis identifies broad associations and isolated purchases dominating recommendations, while existing embedding and margin probes cannot measure which history evidence drives ranking. At initial research progress, controlled diagnostics offer an inexpensive basis for choosing subsequent model changes.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Call view.model.eval() and restore its prior mode afterward. Preserve existing scoring hooks, adding an optional architecture-specific intervention hook for explicit position-preserving attention masks. If unsupported, report the intervention as unavailable rather than silently replacing it with deletion. Construct TF–IDF clusters and popularity counts solely from permitted training histories and titles/descriptions. Use fixed random seeds, bounded user samples, paired controls, and user-level uncertainty estimates. Report missing metadata, unmatched histories, and empty observations as unavailable with counts. Preserve all four dataset routes, os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the pinned evaluator. This diagnostic alone requires no predictor architecture change; any later model change must update the predictor writer.
idea.pseudocode: For each category, sample eligible training users with a fixed seed. Build recent repeated-interest clusters from training-item text. Cache unperturbed scores over a fixed diagnostic candidate set. For each cluster, create several equal-size control masks matched by position bins and training popularity; retain original position indices in every condition. Score evidence masks, control masks, isolated-event masks, and separate order perturbations through the actual trained model. Measure paired original-target rank changes where a legal held-out target is available, plus recommendation overlap for training-user diagnostics. Aggregate within category, bootstrap users within category, and return metrics with definitions, eligibility counts, and explicit missing values. Use only host-computed macro validation HR@10 for model selection.

originality.positive: Combines interest-specific interventions, matched corruption controls, and architecture-compatible probes in a focused diagnostic.
originality.negative: History perturbation and matched controls are established techniques; the contribution is their careful adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish weak interest aggregation from isolated-event sensitivity and guide targeted architecture or objective ablations.
future_potential.negative: Text clusters approximate interests, and diagnostic improvements may not translate into higher validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing scoring hooks and requires no additional trained encoder or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct position-preserving masking and balanced control matching require architecture-specific checks.

related_work.title: CETRec (2025)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes separate treatment of recency and relative interaction order through counterfactual tuning.
limitations: Its LLM recommender setting does not establish effectiveness for SASRec on the four matched Amazon datasets.
It does not validate the proposed matched masking protocol.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes properties of sampled evaluation, including agreement with full-catalog ranking and robustness to exposure bias.
limitations: Does not make supplementary full-catalog diagnostics interchangeable with the pinned sampled benchmark.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Product Recommendation Guidelines
contributions: Provides a vocabulary separating substitutes, complements, unrelated items, and unassessable relationships, including compatibility distinctions.
limitations: Relationship judgments require supporting information and cannot establish current ownership or replacement intent.
Sparse titles and descriptions may require frequent abstention.
